If the constant of a spring is $k$, and if the spring is compressed by a distance $x$ from its normal state, then the potential energy stored in it is,

$$V = \frac{1}{2}kx^2$$

If a spring is compressed or expanded by an amount $x$, it will exert a force of $F = -kx$, using this equation it is possible to find out the relation, $V = \frac{1}{2}kx^2$. Can you find it? (Since the force depends on the length of the spring, so calculate the average force and multiply it by the total distance.)

**Question:** A body of mass $10\text{ kg}$ falls on a spring with a velocity of $10\text{ m/s}$. If the spring constant $k = 100,000\text{ J/m}^2$, what is the compression?

**Answer:** Kinetic energy of the object,

$$\frac{1}{2}mv^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 10^2\text{ J} = 500\text{ J}$$

This energy will compress the spring, that is,

$$\frac{1}{2}kx^2 = 500\text{ J}$$

therefore,

$$x^2 = \frac{2 \times 500}{100,000}\text{ m}^2 = \frac{1}{100}\text{ m}^2$$

$$x = 0.1\text{ m}$$
